column4: The national team wins the World Cup. Millions celebrate at the Obelisk and across the country; for a few weeks nobody talks about inflation.
The worst drought in sixty years wipes out the harvest. Billions of dollars in exports are lost.
Extraordinary rains burst rivers and streams. Thousands evacuated and whole neighbourhoods under water.
A grid failure leaves millions without power in the middle of a heatwave. Residents block streets with bonfires.
For the first time since his election, the Argentine Pope tours the country. Huge crowds and a message about poverty no one can ignore.
A newspaper investigation exposes bribes in public works. A driver's notebooks record every bag of cash.
An international miner announces a record investment in a salt flat in the Puna.
With the country cheap in dollars, tourists arrive from all over the world. Bariloche, Iguazú and Buenos Aires are packed.
With prices soaring, crowds loot supermarkets in Greater Buenos Aires, Rosario and Córdoba.
Hundreds of thousands of students, lecturers and families march in defence of public universities. It is one of the largest protests in decades.

column3: An Argentine film wins the Oscar
column4: Argentine cinema wins the award for best international feature once again.
Fire spreads through native forests in the Andes. Firefighters from across the country battle the flames.
The trade surplus breaks records: more dollars come in than in any year in history.
A train with failed brakes crashes into a terminal station. Years of poor maintenance are exposed.
Heads of state from around the world arrive in Buenos Aires for a G20 summit.
The President promotes a cryptocurrency on social media that crashes minutes later. Thousands of investors lose their savings and the opposition calls for impeachment.
Recordings leak of a former official describing a bribery scheme in the purchase of medicines for disabled people.
A batch of contaminated fentanyl causes dozens of deaths in hospitals. Controls on the laboratory are found to have failed.

column3: Devastating storm in a southern Buenos Aires city
column4: Historic rainfall floods a port city within hours: there are deaths, thousands evacuated and entire neighbourhoods destroyed.
The first Latin American Pope dies in Rome. The country declares national mourning and millions bid farewell to the man who made the poor his cause.
Washington announces a 20 billion dollar swap line and buys pesos in the market to halt a run before the elections.
The country suffers the worst dengue epidemic in its history: overwhelmed emergency rooms, repellent shortages and a row over the vaccine.
Extreme cold sends demand soaring: gas is cut to factories and CNG filling stations while LNG cargoes are rushed in.
Air traffic controllers strike over pay: hundreds of flights cancelled over a long weekend.
After years of drug violence, murders in Rosario fall to a two-decade low thanks to the federal operation.
An international agency upgrades Argentina's sovereign rating. Country risk breaks through a new low.
A historic factory on the outskirts of Buenos Aires closes, leaving hundreds out of work. The workers camp at the gate.
Tanks cross a border in Eastern Europe. Grain and energy markets go wild.

column3: The Strait of Hormuz is closed
column4: War in the Gulf blocks a fifth of the world's oil. Brent tops 120 dollars; Asian refineries ask for Argentine crude.
Washington announces tariffs on the whole world and China retaliates. Argentine steel and aluminium are hit.
The Federal Reserve raises its rate for the first time in years. Argentine bonds fall and country risk rebounds.
The real collapses and Brazil enters recession. Argentine car plants suspend shifts.
A poor US harvest and Chinese demand push soybeans to a ten-year high.
A new respiratory virus spreads across every continent. Borders close.
World stock markets fall 20% in a week. Funds go bust and credit freezes.
A new crisis in Venezuela pushes thousands of families south. Many reach Buenos Aires.
The European Parliament ratifies the Mercosur agreement. Beef, wine and lemon producers celebrate; industry worries.
Beijing closes its largest purchase of Argentine soybeans in years amid its trade war with the US.
The bubble of a heavily promoted cryptocurrency has burst. Thousands of self-employed people lost their savings and now demand regulation of digital currencies.
The bubble of a heavily promoted cryptocurrency has burst. Thousands of self-employed people lost their savings and now demand regulation of digital currencies.
A single automated trade sent Argentine shares into a tailspin within minutes. Economists call for urgent rules on automated trading.
Crime is so high that a well-known TV host shot a relative at home, mistaking them for a burglar.
Journalists published the database of a foreign accounting firm: thousands of wealthy Argentines were hiding their money in tax havens.
A showgirl claims she had an affair with you and was paid for her silence out of campaign funds, which is a crime. The afternoon TV shows talk of nothing else.
Central Bank staff were swapping new banknotes for fake ones. If the institution guarding the currency is corrupt, how can people trust the peso?
The public employees' unions are striking over pay. Paperwork grinds to a halt nationwide.

column3: Oil spill on the Patagonian coast
column4: A spill has wiped out local fishing and left coastal towns without a livelihood; people are starting to move to the cities.
Federal courts have arrested officials accused of embezzling public funds. Corruption is no longer protected.
Hundreds of thousands of residents have no safe drinking water: to save money the municipality switched water source and it corroded the lead pipes.
An official you appointed praised a bloodthirsty dictator in a speech. Human rights groups demand their resignation.
An earthquake has struck Mendoza and San Juan. Few lives were lost, but the damage will slow the regional economy for a while.
Money a former official had hidden in foreign bank accounts has been brought home.
The courts have sentenced former military leaders of the last dictatorship. Another step for Memory, Truth and Justice.
Hidden-camera footage exposed conditions in several meatpacking plants. Cheap meat has a cost nobody wanted to see.
A foreign former spy granted asylum here was poisoned with radioactive material in a Buenos Aires restaurant.
Petrol stations have run dry: domestic production cannot keep up and imports are stuck.

column3: Argentine series is a global hit
column4: A domestic series is a worldwide sensation: over a hundred countries have bought it and it is winning awards everywhere.
Congress has refused to pass the budget and public services are suspended for a month. Your policies lack enough support in Congress.
A record heatwave is causing fires and several deaths. The country is not prepared for such temperatures.
An international report ranks the country among the most corrupt in the Americas. Corruption holds everything back: investment, services and trust.
An electrical fault caused a deadly fire in a social housing tower. Poor construction and lack of inspections made the tragedy worse.
Property prices in dollars hit a record. A sign the economy is getting stronger.
Prices are falling again. Multiple-home buyers and foreign investors had pushed them beyond what people could afford.
Rising irregular immigration across the northern borders is provoking complaints from conservatives.

column3: Top prize for an Argentine writer
column4: An Argentine writer has won the world's most prestigious literary prize for a novel set in the country.
An international report ranks the country among the least corrupt in the Americas. Business can thrive and people trust more.
A protester set themselves on fire in Plaza de Mayo against the government and died. Their death unleashes a wave of anger.
A newspaper revealed rigged tenders in the armed forces used to divert public money into private accounts. An investigation is under way.
A collapse at a mine in the Andes killed dozens of miners. Safety standards are being investigated, but people see it as too little, too late.
A major multinational will set up its regional headquarters here, drawn by the skilled workforce and stability.
Banks, media and government websites were knocked out by a massive foreign cyberattack.

column3: Argentina crash out of the World Cup
column4: The national team has been knocked out earlier than expected. The players are slammed everywhere and the country is in football mourning.

column3: Nobel Peace Prize for an Argentine
column4: An Argentine who promotes democracy at home and abroad has received the Nobel Peace Prize. A huge international endorsement.
Buenos Aires hosted the Olympic Games flawlessly. The whole world was watching.
A Vaca Muerta pipeline crosses land owned by an indigenous community, which opposes it over the environmental impact and has won international support.
A plane belonging to the national airline crashed with no survivors. Poor maintenance is blamed, and so is the state.
An unarmed young man from a poor neighbourhood was shot dead by police. Human rights groups and his community march for justice.
Police killed several protesters during a march. Legal or not, the crackdown is condemned at home and abroad.
The world's richest company made billions here and paid no tax at all thanks to accounting tricks.
Argentine scientists have developed a lithium battery with twice the capacity. It could change industry worldwide.
A well-known company has cancelled its stock market debut. More and more firms prefer not to list here.
The latest Argentine tech startup has listed on the stock exchange and investors scrambled to buy shares.
It emerged that your partner took a private jet to go shopping in Miami. An abuse of power voters will not easily forgive.
A foreign head of state has called off a visit, citing insecurity and instability. You look weak to the world.
A storm has destroyed a key stretch of railway. Underinvestment in infrastructure is plain to see.
A foreign tourist was killed in a robbery. The story is everywhere and hurts tourism.
An Argentine diplomat has been chosen as Secretary-General of the United Nations.
Huge crowds of women marched on Congress against inequality and gender violence. They are half the electorate.
UNESCO has declared a new Argentine site a World Heritage Site.
Mobs attacked foreign-owned shops, accusing them of taking jobs. The victims sheltered in churches and police stations.
Rating agencies have downgraded the debt. Country risk rises and investors will think twice before coming.
